knownGaps: MORTGAGE15US is unavailable before 1991-08; its lone 1991-08-30 observation is retained raw but excluded from the monthly average, so normalised coverage starts 1991-09.
The normalised file ends 2026-06. Later raw mortgage observations are retained but excluded by the final-month alignment rule.
Freddie Mac changed the Primary Mortgage Market Survey methodology on 2022-11-17; pre/post observations are not perfectly method-homogeneous.
Mortgage rates are not seasonally adjusted; CPIAUCSL is seasonally adjusted.

CPIAUCSL has a blank source observation for 2025-10 because BLS did not publish the all-items October 2025 index after the lapse in appropriations; the normalised cell is intentionally blank and is not interpolated.
Freddie Mac mortgage-rate data carried by FRED is copyrighted and requires source citation; keep the manifest citations with any redistributed snapshot.

housingSnapshot.retrievalMode: pinned raw files; build is offline

zillowZhvi.cut: all homes, middle tier, smoothed and seasonally adjusted

housingSnapshot.matchingRule: match only when the state displayed in Zillow's metro name is included in FHFA states and the normalized Zillow core city is the leading official-name core (including a leading slash alias); one explicit official lookup override maps Poughkeepsie to CBSA 28880; exclude any MSAD candidate rather than pair whole-MSA rent with division price
knownGaps: Zillow ZORI begins in 2015 and starts later for many metros, so it sets the overlap horizon even though FHFA and mortgage-rate data are older.
FHFA publishes Metropolitan Division series instead of a whole-MSA series for split MSAs. Zillow whole-MSA rows for those places are excluded until an explicit, weighted aggregation is sourced.
The conservative automatic matcher leaves name changes and non-leading-city aliases unmatched instead of guessing. Any future manual override must cite an official geography source.
The normalised value files contain only the 367 matched whole-MSA geographies. metros.csv retains every excluded and unmatched Zillow row so dropped geography remains auditable.
FHFA all-transactions HPI is quarterly, not seasonally adjusted, and measures price change rather than a price level. ZORI is monthly and smoothed but not seasonally adjusted in this snapshot.

ZHVI supplies a monthly dollar home-value level and is smoothed and seasonally adjusted. It is a modeled typical value, not a transaction median, and its seasonality treatment differs from this ZORI cut.
National 30-year mortgage-rate coverage is 1971-04..2026-06; it does not constrain any matched overlap window here.

assumptions: Matched whole-MSA metros only, 2018-01 through 2026-03: 241 metros carry every month of rent, home value, price index and mortgage rate. Thirteen split metros, including many of the largest, are excluded rather than mismatched; fourteen more clear C4's span-based bar but have missing months inside the span, and are excluded rather than interpolated.
Home value is Zillow's ZHVI (modelled typical home, middle tier); rent is Zillow's ZORI (modelled typical asking rent). They are not the same physical property, and their seasonal treatments differ.

Both households spend exactly the same cash every month. Whoever pays less that month invests the difference in the S&P Composite with dividends reinvested. The buyer's surplus account exists for the months a locked payment beats rising rents.
The buyer puts 20% down, pays 2.5% closing on the way in and 7% selling costs on the way out. Sale costs land only at exit, which is what makes the holding period load-bearing.
Ownership costs run monthly against the current home value: 1% property tax, 0.5% insurance, 1% maintenance per year. The C5 memo carries the cited ranges; the sensitivity bundles rerun them.
30-year fixed at that month's Freddie Mac survey rate. No points, no PMI, no refinancing ever - a 20% down borrower who never refinances through 2020-21 is a conservative construction for buying.
No federal tax benefit in the base case: most filers take the standard deduction. An itemizer scenario is a panel item, not a base assumption.
Everything runs in nominal dollars; the verdict is the wealth gap as a share of the starting home price, which is unit-free.
Start months overlap heavily within a metro and metros move together, so thousands of runs are far fewer independent trials than they look.
